comparator.name: Dutch Languages and Cultures
comparator.sourceNotes: The degree offers Dutch Language and Culture and Frisian Language and Culture. This example follows the Dutch track for September 2026 entrants. Its second- and third-year courses begin in 2027–2028 and 2028–2029.

components.note: Complete workshops in two different areas chosen from literature, linguistics and language use.

components.name: Bachelor’s Thesis in Dutch Studies
components.note: Before starting, complete at least 50 EC from year one, earn at least 100 EC in the degree overall, and pass Research Approaches.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target covers a current bachelor with two equally formal, language-specific tracks: Dutch Language and Culture and Frisian Language and Culture. Current official evidence does not establish either as more representative, broader or less specialized. The Dutch Language and Culture track is therefore selected because it is listed first in the current official regulation, applying the neutral official-order tie-break before any UCR fit assessment.
